title: Room Booking API
statement:
A conference center has an unlimited supply of rooms, each identified by an integer `id`. Every room starts completely free. You must implement the booking API `bookApi(id, startTime, endTime)` and process a sequence of booking requests in order.

A request asks to reserve room `id` for the half-open time slot `[startTime, endTime)`. The request **succeeds** (return `true`) if the slot does not overlap any booking that was **already accepted** for the same room, and the booking is then recorded. Otherwise it **fails** (return `false`) and nothing is recorded.

- Two slots overlap if they share any moment of time. Slots that only touch, such as `[10, 20)` and `[20, 30)`, do **not** overlap.
- Bookings of different rooms never interfere with each other.
- Failed requests have no effect on later requests.

For every request print whether it succeeded.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `q`, the number of requests.
Each of the next `q` lines contains three integers `id`, `startTime` and `endTime`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines. Line `i` is `true` if request `i` succeeds and `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: Room 1 is free, so `[10,20)` is accepted. `[15,25)` overlaps it, so it fails and is not recorded. `[20,30)` only touches the first booking, so it is accepted. Room 2 has no bookings, so `[10,20)` is accepted there. `[5,10)` touches `[10,20)` in room 1 and is accepted. `[0,40)` overlaps the bookings of room 1 and fails.
The second request is identical to the first accepted booking, so it overlaps and fails. `[2,3)` only touches `[1,2)` and is accepted.

hints: Each room is independent, so keep a separate collection of accepted slots per room id (a hash map from id to its slots).
Accepted slots in one room never overlap, so if you keep them sorted by start time, only the neighbours of the new slot can conflict with it.
Binary search the position of `startTime`: the slot before it must end at or before `startTime`, and the slot after it must start at or after `endTime`.
